items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: And it just happened Wilbur DeParis, the trombone player

ctx.x: So we go to the party that night, and at the party... I mean, it was a nice party the girls give us. Drinkin', one-thing-and-another, and some fellows go in the back and start a little nickel-and-dime crap game. Well, you know how them little crap games, they grow... It soon got to be dollars, and five dollars and ten dollars, whatever you could afford to bet. I got clean so quick... I'm always in them games, and I start all the games, and I'm always the first one to get broke -- and I got broke. Which didn't…

Well, I got broke, and the different fellows, they start to cuttin' out, goin' home, this-that-and-the-other. And the first thing I know, the party was over and I almost didn't get back to Los Angeles, to where I lived there. And it just happened Wilbur DeParis, the trombone player, he saw me out in the street trying to get a cab or something... I wasn't trying to get a cab because I didn't have any money. But I was trying to get in to where I lived. And he had transportation, so he picked me up and brought me…
